name: Sprinto — Discovery to Shipped Internal Tool (full structural sketch, D1–D12)

nodes.name: Schedule Trigger — Weekly, After the QCM
nodes.notes: D1: batch, not continuous. Continuous discovery floods the reviewer and turns the approval queue into the bottleneck. A weekly batch produces one reviewable shortlist and paces the whole pipeline.

nodes.name: Form Submission Endpoint (secondary input)
nodes.notes: D1 secondary input: optional structured form, filed anytime. Catches what nobody says out loud in the QCM, and is the entry point for the below-threshold high-conviction route (D3). Persists to a store — does NOT trigger the pipeline (batch, not stream).

nodes.name: Persist to Candidate Store
nodes.notes: PLATFORM: append-only store, swept by the weekly trigger. Batch-not-stream lives in this wiring, not just in prose.

nodes.name: SCOUT — Normalise QCM + Form Inputs
nodes.notes: D4: does NOT judge or filter. A filter with no human oversight is exactly where good ideas silently die — same principle as the below-threshold escape hatch, one step earlier. Output: structured candidates with evidence links back to the raw source.

nodes.name: SCOUT — Cluster Similar Candidates
nodes.notes: D9 test case 7 (a real gap found stress-testing this design): two teams raised the same problem in different words, scored separately, neither cleared 25%, both died. Fix: group semantically similar candidates and COMBINE their pools before scoring. Clustering itself is an LLM/embedding job — OPEN, stubbed here as fuzzy title matching.

nodes.name: SCORER — Threshold Check (25%, time-decayed)
nodes.notes: D2/D3: 25% of the ROLE POOL (combined across the cluster), weight halving every quarter. 'A threshold may deprioritise an idea. It may never silently kill one' — below-threshold routes differently, it is never discarded.

values.content:
You are the Scorer. Return TWO separate scores, never collapsed into one number: impactScore (0-100, direct hours/speed + indirect morale/retention effect of visibly fixing reported problems) and sentimentScore (0-100, distress level). Also assess recurrence, automatability (rule-shaped scores high; judgment-shaped work is a bad first target), and blastRadius.

Treat self-reported affected/stress ratings as WEAK, GAMEABLE signals - people anchor differently and scores inflate once staff learn high numbers get action. Cross-check against reported hours lost and recurrence.

Emit confidence (0-1) and unresolvedAssumptions - the system is allowed to be uncertain, but never allowed to hide it.

Reply JSON only: {impactScore, sentimentScore, recurrence, automatability, blastRadius, confidence, unresolvedAssumptions:[string]}

nodes.name: SCORER — Impact + Sentiment Scores
nodes.notes: Two scores, always kept separate — impact (value of fixing) and sentiment (distress), plus confidence + unresolved assumptions. Sentiment is a known-gameable weak signal, cross-checked against hours lost, per D2's stated limitation.

nodes.name: SCORER — Merge Scores into State
nodes.notes: The LLM node replaces the payload, so candidate state is explicitly re-attached here — the concrete answer to 'how does state carry across agents'. Low-confidence output is routed to needs_context, not passed downstream.

nodes.name: SCORER — Rank + Cap Shortlist (top 5/week)
nodes.notes: D6/D10 fail-safe #3: an uncapped shortlist against a reviewer's limited time grows a queue forever. Below-cap candidates PERSIST with their scores and re-enter next week's ranking — never dropped.

values.outputKey: Route B — below threshold, high conviction

options.renameFallbackOutput: Persists — capped or below threshold, re-enters next week

nodes.name: Switch — Route to Gate 1 (two entry routes)
nodes.notes: D3: two DELIBERATE routes converging on the same gate, not one path with a rare exception. Route A: sanity-check a strong signal, usually a fast approve. Route B: a genuine judgment call, overriding a threshold. Both reach a human — the design's central promise: a threshold may deprioritise, it may never silently kill.

nodes.name: PERSIST — Capped/Below-threshold, Re-enters Next Week
nodes.notes: D6/D10: not a dead end. Score and evidence carry forward; re-scored against next week's fresh signal (recurrence weighting) rather than lost.

nodes.name: 🔶 ESCALATE — Low Confidence / Blocked
nodes.notes: D8: 'The system is allowed to be uncertain. It is never allowed to hide it.' Routes here with the SPECIFIC unresolved question attached — not 'I'm stuck', but e.g. 'role-pool size unknown for security-analyst; which team owns that number?' Fed by every low-confidence branch in the pipeline (threshold, scoring, validation), not only this one entry point.

nodes.name: GATE 1 — Wait: Worth our time? (AI Lead)
nodes.notes: 🛑 REVIEWER: AI implementation team lead. QUESTION: Is this worth our time? ACTION: pick from ranked shortlist, or reject. WHY HERE: cheap decision before an expensive artifact — writing the PRD first would ANCHOR the reviewer, a polished PRD makes a mediocre idea look legitimate. Non-blocking: other candidates keep scoring while this one waits.

nodes.name: GATE 1 — Record Decision
nodes.notes: Appends to the decision log — who, when, what. Feeds the Rubber-Stamp Detector and makes gate rejection rate (D11) measurable after the fact.

nodes.name: RUBBER-STAMP DETECTOR
nodes.notes: D10 fail-safe #1: gate rejection rate is a metric, but a metric with no mechanism is decorative. If a reviewer approves N consecutive items in under X seconds each, flag it. Fed by all three gates' decision-record nodes, not just Gate 1.

nodes.name: Terminated at Gate 1 (logged with reason)
nodes.notes: Where the loop exits early. Logged, not discarded — rejection rate too low signals rubber-stamping, too high signals discovery is broken.

values.content:
You are the Definer. Draft a PRD grounded only in the evidence supplied - do not invent requirements the evidence doesn't support; list gaps in openQuestions instead. A plausible-but-wrong PRD is the worst failure mode here: it looks fine and ships the wrong thing.

If this is a retry, validationErrors from the previous attempt are attached - fix those specific issues.

Write the problem statement in the reporters' own words so Gate 2 (the requester) can tell at a glance whether it was understood.

Reply JSON only: {problem, users:[string], scope:{inScope:[string], outOfScope:[string]}, requirements:[string], successCriteria:[string], claimedTimeSavingHrsPerWeek:number, openQuestions:[string], confidence}

nodes.name: DEFINER — Draft PRD
nodes.notes: Only runs after Gate 1, so no compute is spent on ideas not worth doing. Grounded only in Scout's evidence — an invented requirement here is exactly the plausible-but-wrong-PRD failure mode (D9), the worst case because it looks fine and ships wrong.

nodes.name: VALIDATE — Schema + Semantic Check
nodes.notes: D7, the strongest technical point in the design: shape validation alone is insufficient — a well-formed JSON PRD can still describe a different problem than the one raised (same class of bug as a tensor that passes an 'is this 2D' check while being semantically wrong). Checks whether the PRD's user list matches the reporting role-pool and whether claimed savings fall near reported hours. Retries once with the error fed back; escalates on second failure.

nodes.name: VALIDATE — Outcome? (pass / retry once / escalate)
nodes.notes: Three outcomes, so this is a Switch and not an IF. An IF has only two branches, which would leave 'escalate' nowhere to go and silently loop every repeat failure back into the Definer forever. Retry count comes from $runIndex, because a counter stored on the candidate resets on every loop-back.

values.content:
You are the PRD self-critique checker. Grade the PRD against a checklist BEFORE any human sees it, so obvious gaps never waste human attention: are specific users named (not 'some users'), are success criteria measurable (numbers, not adjectives), is scope explicitly bounded (has an outOfScope list).

Reply JSON only: {passed:boolean, usersNamed:boolean, successCriteriaMeasurable:boolean, scopeBounded:boolean, gaps:[string]}

nodes.name: SELF-CRITIQUE — PRD Checklist
nodes.notes: Named users? Measurable success criteria? Bounded scope? Runs BEFORE any human sees the PRD, so obvious gaps never consume Gate 2's scarce attention. Humans are the last catch here, not the first.

nodes.name: SELF-CRITIQUE — Merge into State
nodes.notes: Same state re-attachment pattern as every other LLM boundary in this pipeline.

nodes.name: GATE 2 — Wait: Understood correctly? (Requester)
nodes.notes: 🛑 REVIEWER: the person who RAISED the problem, not the AI lead — only they know whether the PRD describes their actual pain. QUESTION: Did the system understand the problem correctly? ACTION: edit and approve. WHY HERE: the cheapest possible place to catch a misread — every downstream step compounds this error. This is the costly review, deliberately placed in the middle where catching an error saves the most work.

nodes.name: GATE 2 — Apply Requester Edits
nodes.notes: Edited fields are logged individually — repeated edits to the same field signal the Definer prompt is systematically wrong, not just this one PRD.

nodes.name: DESIGNER — Generate Wireframe [platform capability]
nodes.notes: OUTSIDE N8N'S SCOPE. PLATFORM: 2-3 wireframe variants from the approved PRD. Variants, not one design — choosing beats blank-page review, and taste/internal convention isn't inferable from a PRD alone.

nodes.name: BUILDER — Build App on Platform [platform capability]
nodes.notes: OUTSIDE N8N'S SCOPE. PLATFORM: assembles the app from the approved PRD + design. D8: on an ambiguous PRD, builds the SMALLEST DEFENSIBLE VERSION and flags the ambiguity at Gate 3 — stopping wastes the run, guessing big is worse than guessing small, and the flag ensures a human sees the ambiguity before anything ships.

nodes.name: GATE 3 — Wait: Safe to ship? (AI Lead)
nodes.notes: 🛑 REVIEWER: AI implementation team lead. QUESTION: Is it safe to put this live? ACTION: one-click approve to ship. WHY HERE: blast radius, not quality — anything touching real internal data or another team's workflow needs a human first. ASYMMETRIC DEFAULT: this gate always defaults to HALT on timeout, unlike earlier low-risk gates.

nodes.name: GATE 3 — Record Decision
nodes.notes: Surfaces any ambiguity flag the Builder attached (D8) directly in front of the reviewer at the moment of the ship decision.

nodes.name: Halted at Gate 3 — Not Deployed
nodes.notes: Timeout or rejection both land here. Nothing ships without an explicit human yes.

nodes.name: DEPLOY — Ship to Internal Server [platform capability]
nodes.notes: OUTSIDE N8N'S SCOPE. PLATFORM: deploys the app and starts usage instrumentation — the input the 30-day review below depends on.

nodes.name: Schedule Trigger — 30 Days Post-Deploy
nodes.notes: D10 fail-safe #2: the pipeline used to end at deploy with nothing catching a tool that ships and turns out useless. The 30-day usage metric becomes a TRIGGER, not just a number in a report.

nodes.name: 30-DAY REVIEW — Still in Use?
nodes.notes: D11: the headline metric is % of shipped tools still in use after 30 days — deliberately not 'apps shipped', which rewards volume over usefulness.

nodes.name: Confirmed Useful — No Action
nodes.notes: Tool earns its keep. No human action needed.

nodes.name: RETIRE / ROLLBACK — Flagged for Human Decision
nodes.notes: PLATFORM: unused tool flagged to the AI implementation lead for retire-or-rollback. The metric now has a mechanism attached to it, not just a dashboard number.

parameters.content:
## Sprinto — Discovery to Shipped Internal Tool
### STRUCTURAL SKETCH — NOT A RUNNABLE WORKFLOW

Implements DESIGN_DECISIONS_FINAL.md (D1–D12) in full.
Read left to right; escalation/review branches sit below the main line.
Every node's **notes** field (document icon) carries the reasoning —
that is where the defensible content lives, open them.

Raw inputs stubbed, LLM nodes uncredentialed, platform-capability
steps are NoOp placeholders. This exists to pressure-test hand-offs
and to illustrate the submission, not to run.

### TWO ENTRY ROUTES INTO GATE 1

**Route A — high-signal:** ≥25% of the (clustered) role-pool reports it in-window. Human is sanity-checking a strong signal.

**Route B — below threshold, high-conviction:** a form submission carries real numbers (hours lost, concrete description). Human is making a genuine judgment call, overriding the threshold.

Both converge on the SAME gate. 'A threshold may deprioritise an idea. It may never silently kill one.'

**GATE 1** — AI lead
Q: *Is this worth our time?*
Action: pick from shortlist, or reject.

**GATE 2** — the requester (not the AI lead)
Q: *Did we understand it correctly?*
Action: edit and approve.

**GATE 3** — AI lead
Q: *Is it safe to put this live?*
Action: one-click approve. Defaults to HALT on timeout.

### PLATFORM CAPABILITIES CLUSTER
Designer, Builder, Deploy are NoOp here — capabilities provided by the internal low-code platform, outside n8n's scope. Assumed per the brief: the platform can run multi-step agentic workflows, hold state, request human input mid-run, and deploy a simple app.

### STATE MODEL
One versioned `UseCase` record, read and written by every agent — nothing passed as loose context. Accumulates evidence → scores → PRD → design → build artifacts, plus an **append-only human decision log** (who, when, what changed).

Why: reject at step 4, re-run ONE agent, not the whole pipeline. And at a compliance company, the decision log means 'why did we build this' has an actual answer months later — auditability is not decoration.

### THE HUMAN IS NEVER ON THE CRITICAL PATH
While one candidate waits at a gate, ingestion, scoring and ranking keep running for every other candidate. A slow reviewer delays one item, never the pipeline.
